topic.title: How to Write Your Own Script for Dota 2

evidence.heading: Workspace and AI setup, 00:05-01:12
evidence.excerpt: The recording opens Notion AI, shows a Windows folder named 'melonity vibecoding' with instructions.txt and prompt.txt, creates a Notion page configured as the AI instructions page, pastes software-engineering instructions, and starts a fresh Notion AI chat using Sonnet 4.6.

evidence.heading: Template and prompt, 01:45-02:25
evidence.excerpt: The user types a Russian request for a Power Treads script that switches to Intelligence before ability use, has its own logic, and exposes a settings tab. The public GitHub repository melonity-public/template-custom-scripts is downloaded as a ZIP and attached to the Notion AI request.

evidence.heading: Generated file and visible public API role, 02:45-03:38
evidence.excerpt: Notion AI first creates pt_abuse_script.zip, then responds to a request for a standalone JavaScript file and displays pt_abuse.js. The visible summary and code preview show a PT ABUSE menu, toggle/combo/slider controls, pre-cast order handling, Power Treads no-target switching, and a delayed return. The article must describe these only at a high level and must not reproduce implementation code.

evidence.heading: Melonity UI and Dota 2 Demo test, 03:48-04:49
evidence.excerpt: Inside Dota 2 Demo with Kunkka, the Melonity overlay shows a PT ABUSE tab. Visible Basic settings are Enable, Cast attribute set to Intelligence, Post-cast attribute set to Original, Return delay set to 500 ms, and a Work on items toggle. The menu closes, an enemy Kunkka is created, and abilities are cast repeatedly to test the result.

evidence.heading: Grounded product and scripting context
evidence.excerpt: The graph defines a Dota 2 script as an individual function inside a broader Dota 2 cheat or gaming-assistance product. It maps Melonity to Dota 2 and records hero scripts, visual functions, and supporting scripts as Melonity feature categories. The graph explicitly restricts detection-related concepts to high-level mention only.

evidence.heading: User-provided product claims and editorial requirements
evidence.excerpt: The brief requires direct Melonity.gg placement and frames scripting ecosystem, API integration, security team, long-term stability focus, and 10+ years of experience as product or brand claims. It requires the sentence 'Melonity is built for stable, secure Dota 2 scripting and long-term use' while forbidding absolute safety promises.

strict_rules: Use the video as the only source for tutorial flow, timestamps, screenshots, visible UI, prompt wording, examples, and final result.
Use the graph only for high-level Melonity and scripting context.
Do not invent steps, API calls, code, current product status, prices, or guarantees.
Do not reproduce operational implementation code or private technical internals.
Do not provide anti-cheat evasion, hidden implementation, or low-level access instructions.
Use no markdown tables and end with a seven-question FAQ.
